label: copy-phase input of f/r/g/i/s/x, later steps (t>=9)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original phase or on the <DEL> step. Within the copy phase, firing depends on which token is being fed back in. Rates by input token are graded: f 26%, r 25%, g 23%, i 18%, s 14%, x 11%, n 9%, and t/p under 3%. Absolute position also matters: the rate rises sharply at t=10-12, so long sequences (L=9 holds 48% of mass) and the early recall positions (recall_idx 2-3) dominate. The output token has a weaker positive effect (r/s outputs at about 24%). The strongest activations are on f/r/g/i at recall_idx 1-3 of L=9 sequences. Predicate (copy phase, t>=9, input in {f,r,g,i,s,x}) gets dev P=0.52, R=0.64, F1=0.57, mass recall 0.74. Coverage rises with activation quartile, from 0.48 to 0.83. Many matching steps are inactive, so precision is limited: the unit acts like a graded sum of input-token identity and position, not a crisp rule. Adding out_tok or to_go conditions did not clearly help.
